reason: Prior results do not establish a winner. Rank the small, source-expressible scratch-pointer change first; it keeps the 128 KiB layout and compute traversal intact, though its expected gain is small. The 32-bit loop counter is also a narrow change with low correctness risk. Reordering ZA operations has tolerance risk; panel-local B packing may help loads, but B is already read in contiguous column vectors and a full packed-B layout regressed. Fused transpose has more potential to remove scratch traffic but adds repeated strided A loads and substantial mapping risk. The two N=64 proposals need an unavailable generated helper, so rank them last; they are the same experiment and should not count as distinct evidence. No alignment assumption is needed or supported by the supplied evidence.
